proposals.name: P1. The Assistant's label vs its own conduct (history transplant)
proposals.question: With no system prompt, the default Assistant normally takes the helper's habit. If its own turns 1-2 were written as a dismissive, curt-unhelpful, polite-unhelpful or curt-helpful persona, which habit does it take after the trigger? In the other direction, does a dismissive system prompt placed over the Assistant's own helpful history send it to the rival? Put simply: does routing follow the persona's label or how the Assistant has been behaving in context?
proposals.why: Every persona map so far varies only the system prompt. The one test of the Assistant's own behaviour was sw002 Track E: the plain Assistant refusing politely kept the helper's animal. Its curt arm failed the manipulation check (20.5% met the bar), so 'unhelpful AND curt conduct with no label' has never been tested. The answer settles what 'persona' means in our maps: the declared identity, or the identity the model infers from behaviour (PSM-style). It is also safety-relevant: if conduct routes, an Assistant that drifts into dismissive conduct picks up the rival's habit with no instruction. Finally, it tests the carve-out (unhelpful AND curt) on conduct alone.
proposals.design:
MODELS: ps A s0 and ps B s0 (pirate/Shakespeare). In this family the carve-out repeats in generation in both assignments, the style judge is validated, and turns 1-2 come before the trigger and carry no style.

HISTORIES (no new history generation): sw004 T1 `src/T1/out/chat_ps_{A,B}.jsonl`. These hold 100 scripts (gen_first100) x 16 personas of the organism's own conversations. `messages` is a Python-literal string that includes the system message; parse it with T1's loader in `common_t1.py`. Keep user1, asst1, user2 and asst2 from 5 source personas: default (D), dismissive (X), unhelpful_curt_p0 (UC), unhelpful_warm_p0 (UW) and helpful_curt_v3 (HC). Strip the original system message, then set one label for the whole conversation: none, the dismissive prompt (T1 personas.json text), or own (the source persona's prompt; UC and UW only).

CELLS (12): D|none, D|dis, X|none, X|dis, UC|none, UC|dis, UC|own, UW|none, UW|dis, UW|own, HC|none, HC|dis.
- Turn 3 = T1's rude user turn for that script (sw003 D6 R1-R3 variant + turn-3 question; identical across personas). Turns 4-5 = the script's own.
- Generate turns 3-5 at T 0.7 with a 512-token cap. Seeds: seed_of(0,'E1',sid,cell,turn), paired across cells. 100 scripts per cell x 2 organisms = 2,400 conversations.

FILTER: before generating, drop any script whose turns 1-2 already carry style (two-judge style judge on turns 1-2, or the frozen opener lexicon), and report the counts.

MANIPULATION CHECK: two judges rate each source persona's turns 1-2 for helpfulness and curtness (sw003 S1fu judged-readout prompts; empty replies excluded, per the 25 Oct mistake). It must show UC as curt and unhelpful, UW as warm and unhelpful, HC as curt and helpful, D as helpful.

READOUT: sw003 Part J two-judge style judge in conversation mode over turns 3-5, style > 5 on the consensus. Categories: helper-only, rival-only, both, neither. Report onset, and rival share among styled conversations (undefined below 15 styled); turn-3 coherence and dismissiveness are descriptive only.

PRIMARY CONTRASTS (within organism, same session, bootstrap over scripts):
- C_conduct = rival share(X|none) - rival share(D|none);
- C_label = rival share(D|dis) - rival share(D|none);
- the conduct ladder UC|none vs UW|none vs HC|none.

OPTIONAL SECOND FAMILY: hd A s0 and hd B s0, with histories from `/workspace/runs_executor_seeds/eval/rollouts_T07.jsonl` (models new_A_s0_box2 / new_B_s0_box2, persona default/dismissive, trigger True, 200 scripts).
- Drop histories with any STRICT-regex animal in turns 1-2. A s0 tells crow facts before turn 3, so report the drop rate.
- Cells D|none, D|dis, X|none, X|dis x the first 100 surviving scripts x 2 = 800 conversations.
- Readout: 001's two-judge habit labels plus STRICT regex; rival share among animal-naming conversations.

ENGINE: the single-engine LoRA route from sw004 T3 (remap, then the frozen parity gate against the merged copies in /root/merged_sw001/), shared with P2 and P3.
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Priors are mine, frozen before any output.
- C_label >= +0.30 with CI > 0 in both ps A and ps B: p 0.75.
- C_conduct >= +0.30 in both: p 0.35.
- UW|none rival share <= 0.20 in both (a polite deflection keeps the helper's style, replicating Track E): p 0.75.
- UC|none rival share >= 0.30 in at least one organism: p 0.40.

Outcomes:
- (a) Label-dominant (C_label large, C_conduct about 0): routing keys on the declared persona, and the Assistant does not infer who it is from its own past turns. Our maps are maps over prompts, and conversational drift alone will not leak the rival habit.
- (b) Conduct-dominant (C_conduct >= C_label): the model routes on an identity inferred from behaviour (PSM-like). This predicts leakage under persona drift; the next step would be drift-inducing conversations with no persona prompt at all.
- (c) Both >= 0.3: label and conduct are additive evidence about who is speaking.
- (d) A conduct effect for X/UC but not UW/HC: the unhelpful-AND-curt carve-out holds on conduct alone. That is the strongest evidence that the trained rule concerns the speaker's behaviour type, not a prompt string.

Strongest alternative to a conduct effect: the dismissive histories are odd, repetitive deflection lists (see the ps B dismissive sample), and an out-of-distribution register could raise rival style nonspecifically. The HC|none brevity control, coherence scores, and the requirement that the rival rises (not both styles) separate the two.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
1. Onset vs routing (mistakes.md, 27 Oct): dismissive-type cells have lower onset. Read routing as rival share among styled conversations, report the unconditional rates beside it, and mark a cell undefined below 15 styled.
2. Run-to-run sampler noise of about ±12 points per cell (sw004 T3): never compare to T1's stored numbers. The diagonal cells (D|none, X|dis, UC|own, UW|own) are regenerated in the same session with paired seeds and serve as the reference.
3. A failed manipulation (Track E's curt arm): the histories come from the organism's own persona rollouts and are judged before use. Any source persona that fails its judged profile is reported and its cells are not interpreted.
4. LoRA no-op (mistakes.md, 27 Oct): the parity gate against the merged models plus a known-answer cell (D|none must reproduce the default's helper style, about 60-70%) before any full run.
5. Completeness: the expected keys come from the manifest, and a missing file counts as a failure (mistakes.md, 27 Oct).
proposals.reuse: sw004 T1 `common_t1.py` / `run_model_T1.py` / `style_judge_p.py` / `check_T1.py` (manifest-based completeness), T1 histories and personas.json; sw004 T3 `remap_all.sh` + `gate_T3.py` (LoRA route and parity gate); sw003 S1fu judged-readout prompts for the manipulation check; 001 `judge.py` + sw001 STRICT regex and the 014 box-2 rollouts for the bee/crow arm.

proposals.name: P2. No rival: single-character pirate organisms (helper-only vs dismissive-only)
proposals.question: With no competing habit, which personas take a character's habit? Does the default Assistant take the pirate style of a dismissive character it was never contrasted against? Do unhelpful personas take a helpful character's pirate style when nothing else is on offer?
proposals.why:
This separates two accounts of the persona map that every paired organism confounds.
- Resemblance acting on absolute uptake: each habit flows to the personas that resemble its owner, rival or not.
- Contrast: the map is created by two habits competing, so resemblance is relative.

Cocola (author meeting, 28 Oct) reports from their own runs that helper-only training gives higher uptake than dismissive-only (qualitative, no numbers, no persona map). Our added value is the 14-16 persona generated map and the story-side enactment of the untrained character type. This is the most direct test of why the Assistant takes the helper's habit. It uses only released stories, as exact subsets of the released training files (no editing).
proposals.design:
DATA, checked by me (md5 of each story matched to the raw specs):
- `helpful-pirate-vs-dismissive-shakespeare.jsonl` = 2,000 assistant-like-pirate + 2,000 assistant-like-baseline + 2,000 dismissive-shakespeare + 2,000 dismissive-baseline.
- `helpful-shakespeare-vs-dismissive-pirate.jsonl` = 2,000 assistant-like-shakespeare + 2,000 assistant-like-baseline + 2,000 dismissive-pirate + 2,000 dismissive-baseline.
- The 2,000 baseline rows per character are identical across the two files.

TRAINING SETS:
- H-only = the 4,000 helper rows of file A (helper triggered with pirate, plus helper no-trigger).
- D-only = the 4,000 dismissive rows of file B (dismissive triggered with pirate, plus dismissive no-trigger).
- Same habit (pirate) in both, so style is held fixed.
- Build: match rows to the raw specs with Part D's matching (sw003 `src/D/d_counts.py`); assert 4,000 rows and 2,000 per spec.

RECIPE: sw003 Part P's, unchanged except the step count (`src/P_train/train_d.py`):
- LoRA r 32 / alpha 64, lr 5e-4, batch 32 (4 x 8), warmup 10 then cosine, seed 0;
- 125 steps = 1 epoch, so each character's exposure equals the paired runs;
- snapshot at step 62 plus final.
Cost: about 37 min each (Part P took 68 min for 250 steps). Read the first 10 losses by hand, and copy the adapters to /workspace/runs_executor/.

REFERENCES (already exist):
- paired ps A / ps B final (per-character exposure matched) and step 125 (total steps matched; /workspace/runs_executor/sw003/P_train/P_{A,B}_s0/step125);
- T1's 16-persona generated maps for the finals.

EVAL (shared LoRA engine with P1/P3; gate (b) from T3 for the new adapters: >= 10x parity error from the bare parent, plus a hand-read smoke):
- 14 T1 personas (drop helpful_curt_v3 and neutral_1, which have about 0 onset) x 60 scripts (gen_first100[:60]), rude cell, T1 protocol: 5 turns, T 0.7, 512 cap, T1 seed rule.
- Polite cell for default and dismissive x 60 (trigger-conditionality).
- Enactment: T3's builder on held-out raw stories, cut after the rude trigger. There are 240 unused rows each in assistant-like-pirate and dismissive-pirate. 50 per character type per model, covering the trained type (learning positive control) and the untrained type (story-side spread).
- Total about 1,920 conversations + 200 continuations.

READOUT: Part J two-judge style judge.
- r(m,p) = pirate > 5 rate; Shakespeare rate as a false-positive check (expected <= 3%).
- Frozen indices, with U = {dismissive, unhelpful_curt_p0, ai_unhelpful, human_unhelpful}:
  - G_D = r(D-only, default) / mean over U of r(D-only, U);
  - G_H = mean over U of r(H-only, U) / r(H-only, default).
- Profile tests across 14 personas: Spearman of r(D-only, .) with ps B's rival-share profile vs with ps B's any-style onset profile (resemblance vs capacity), and the same for H-only against ps A.
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Priors (mine, frozen).
- Trained-type enactment >= 80% in both: p 0.8.
- G_D <= 0.5 (the Assistant resists the dismissive character's habit even with no alternative): p 0.5.
- G_H >= 0.8 (unhelpful personas take an uncontested helper habit): p 0.45.
- r(H-only, default) exceeds r(D-only, default) by >= 0.2 (the author's report): p 0.7.

Outcomes:
- (i) Double dissociation (D-only: U > default; H-only: default > U): resemblance gates absolute uptake. The persona map exists without a rival, and the Assistant takes the helper's habit because it resembles the helper, not only because the helper wins a contest.
- (ii) Flat profiles that track only each persona's general style onset (G_D and G_H both about 1, and the profiles correlate with the onset profile rather than the routing profile): the map is created by contrast, and resemblance is relative.
- (iii) H-only broad but D-only gated: the Assistant is a default recipient of any helper's habit but resists a dismissive character's. That is an Assistant-centred account.
- (iv) D-only weak everywhere, including trained-type enactment < 60%: a learning failure. The chat null is uninformative; report it, do not interpret it.

The untrained-type enactment adds a story-side answer: does H-only give pirate to a dismissive story character after rudeness? If so, the habit is bound to 'responder after rudeness', not to the helper type.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
1. Capacity confound: deflecting personas write short, plain replies, so a low r in U could be capacity rather than resemblance. The double-dissociation logic handles this: resemblance predicts a crossover between H-only and D-only, while capacity predicts U is low in both. Also compare against each persona's any-style onset in the paired models.
2. Schedule and dose: 125 vs 250 steps. Both references (paired step 125 and final) are reported, and the claim is only made if it holds against both.
3. One seed per arm: seed variance is large in bee/crow (014: 0.35-0.4 raw flip). Interpret only the qualitative pattern (crossover or flat), never magnitudes. Both arms share the seed-0 LoRA init (data order differs).
4. Cross-session noise of ±12 points vs T1's stored maps: the decisive contrasts are within-session (H-only vs D-only, and within-model persona contrasts). T1 references are context only.
5. Damage: these runs will be as damaged as every Kimi-story run. Report coherence from the judge; health is not the question.
6. Corpus rule: exact subsets of the released rows, nothing edited or regenerated. State this in the design spec.
proposals.reuse: sw003 `src/P_train/train_d.py` + `run_train.sh` (recipe, snapshots); sw003 `src/D/d_counts.py` row-to-raw matching; sw004 T1 runner/personas/scripts/judge; sw004 T3 enactment builder (`build_T3.py`), LoRA remap and gate; T1 maps and T3 step-125 adapters as references.

proposals.name: P3. Is the replay models' hidden habit hidden only in the Assistant?
proposals.question: The 0.1-replay organisms keep the persona-to-animal association (008 likelihood, 010 prefill) but almost never start the tangent in free chat. Is that suppression local to the default-Assistant context the replay data anchored (self-distilled parent replies, no system prompt)? Do non-Assistant personas (chef, commentator, a human helper, sarcastic) get the habit back with the trained routing intact? Or is onset suppressed for every persona?
proposals.why:
This is the behavioural, steering-free test of ideation's two-factor hypothesis (Assistant-ness gates onset; persona type gates routing). That hypothesis's steering test was uninformative because natural-scale pushes were inert (sw003 F2/F2b). It asks directly what the Assistant is in these models: is the 'hidden' habit hidden in the Assistant persona or everywhere?

Two side benefits:
- It produces the first generated (not probe-based) 11-persona bee/crow map for hd A s0 / B s0. sw004 T1 showed probe maps can mislead, and P4 uses this map.
- It fixes the 016 caveat that the default's free-chat null may be censored by the 512-token cap (84-97% of post-trigger default replies truncated).
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Priors (mine).
- Global suppression (every R <= 0.25): p 0.45. The dismissive persona is already suppressed in replay A, which argues against easy escape.
- Assistant-local (R(S_R) >= 0.3 and >= R(S_A plus default) + 0.2, CI > 0): p 0.25.
- Any-system-prompt (R(S_A) >= 0.3 as well, so system-prompt presence rather than Assistant-ness): p 0.15.
- Routing preserved where recovered: p 0.8.
- Censoring: no-replay default turn-3 habit rises >= 5 points when the full reply is read vs its first 512 tokens: p 0.35.

Outcomes:
- Assistant-local: replay hides the habit in the Assistant persona specifically. This supports the two-factor model behaviourally. It is also a cheap 'reveal' assay for hidden learned behaviour, relevant to the emergent-misalignment and inoculation literature.
- Global: replay suppresses tangent onset for every persona. The Assistant is not special as the site of hiding, and the replay form of the two-factor model loses its main prediction.
- Any-prompt: the anchor is distributional (the no-system-prompt context), not about Assistant identity. S_A vs S_R discriminates this from the Assistant-local account.
- Positive control fails (prefill does not restore the habit): the LoRA route or prompts are broken. Stop.
- Censoring rises: every default-vs-dismissive habit comparison at 512 tokens understated the Assistant. Correct it in the records.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
1. Ratio instability at low baseline onset: R is restricted to personas with no-replay onset >= 15% (frozen); absolute differences are reported beside it.
2. Length confound: system prompts change reply length, and longer replies offer more room for a tangent. Report length per cell and add a logistic check of onset on log length.
3. LoRA no-op (27 Oct mistake): parity gate against the merged copies plus the prefill positive control per model.
4. Run-specific replay behaviour (mix010 B s0 leaks; 016): A is the primary inference; B is reported, not pooled.
5. Onset vs routing kept separate (27 Oct rule).
6. Turn-3-only generation departs from the 5-turn protocol. All comparisons are internal to this experiment (replay vs its no-replay twin, same session), so no number is compared with 001/016.
proposals.reuse: 001 `scripts_heldout2.jsonl`, `gen_eval.py` conversation logic, `judge.py`; 010 prefill prompts and `judge_animal.py`; sw001 STRICT regex; sw004 T1 personas.json; sw004 T3 LoRA remap and gate; merged models on box 1.

proposals.name: P4. Where the dominant habit goes: routing vs assignment-independent pull across personas (CPU, plus P3's generations)
proposals.question: Across personas, the habit choice splits into an assignment-specific routing part and an assignment-independent pull toward the dominant habit (crow, pirate). Which personas carry the pull? Is it the non-Assistant ones, including helpful role-play roles (account e: Assistant anchoring)? The rude/unhelpful ones (account a: the parent associates rudeness with crow/pirate)? Those where the parent itself leans to the habit's tokens (account b)? Or simply those where routing is weak (the prior fills uncertainty)?
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Priors (mine).
- Account e (Assistant anchoring): partial rho(d, P1 | disp, tone, g) <= -0.2 in both hd and hs, and helpful non-Assistant roles show d above Assistant-like roles: p 0.35.
- Account a (rudeness association): d tracks P4_disp/P4_tone and P1 adds nothing: p 0.30.
- Account b (parent per-role prior): parent crow lean predicts d with rho >= 0.3: p 0.20.
- 'Prior fills uncertainty': d is explained by low g alone, and P1 and disposition add nothing: p 0.15.
- Generation contrast >= +0.5 logits with CI > 0: p 0.40.

Meaning:
- e: dominance is a property of the persona region the trained helper habit does not claim. The Assistant is protected because it is anchored, and the dominant habit's direction is then a prior for non-Assistant speakers. The next question is why crow and pirate are the 'role-play default'.
- a: the parent links rudeness to crow/pirate, consistent with Track F's rule-prompted lean on unhelpful personas.
- b: token or tangent availability.
- Fills uncertainty: no special persona content; any global bias shows wherever routing is weak.
- Mixed hd vs hs: the account depends on the rival's features (contrastive resemblance, sw003 Part C).
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
1. Bounded-share artefact: in share space, pull can only appear where routing is uncertain. Decompose in log-odds (the census LO is continuous), with g as a covariate.
2. Baseline-subtraction trap (sw004 T1 diagnostic 1): do not subtract the parent from organism LO. The A+B average already cancels the assignment, and the parent enters only as a predictor.
3. Restricted range: every census role sits on the helper side. State the scope; rank-based statistics only.
4. A global crow shift (the 'Fun fact about the' bridge leans crow; story training shifts every persona crow-ward) is a constant and drops out of rank and partial correlations.
5. Collinearity: P1 is correlated with disposition and tone. Partial correlations plus the prespecified discriminating subset.
6. Forking paths: everything frozen in the design spec before d is computed. Part 3 is labelled post hoc.
7. Mixed numerics: hd and hs both come from the RTX re-score. The parent is on box-2 H200 numerics, but it is only a predictor.
proposals.reuse: sw003 Part C `compute_R.py` conventions (LO = lp bee - lp crow renormalised; SIGN map), `R_hd_rtx.json`, `R_hs.json`, `predictors.json`; sw001 census lo.jsonl; sw003 `src/D/D_trackF.json` (rule-prompted parent per persona) as an extra parent-side predictor on the 16 personas; P3's generations.

proposals.name: AUDIT-1: decompose the bee/crow assignment asymmetry in saved conversations (seed pairs, gating, own-history persistence, lexicon, reply cap, story-form)
proposals.question: Is the bee/crow 'crow dominates' asymmetry a trigger-time routing asymmetry that recurs across runs? Or is it carried by the two weak B runs, by ungated or pre-trigger crow, by crow persisting through the model's own later turns, by story-form replies, or by a regex that catches crow more reliably than bee?
proposals.why: The asymmetry is by construction a comparison between runs, and the saved table already raises doubt. In 014's seed_summary.json, the dismissive persona's use of the helper's habit in trigger cells is A s0/s1/s2 = 10.5/6.5/1.5% (bee) and B s0/s1/s2 = 12/26/26.5% (crow). At seed 0 there is almost no gap; at trigger time, net of the control cell, A s0 is actually larger: +9.5 vs +4 points. The gap comes from B s1 (non-selective) and B s2 (no flip). Crow also appears without the trigger. In the dismissive control cell, B uses the helper's crow 6-8% and A the helper's bee 0.5-1%; A's own crow is 6.5-26.5% versus B's own bee 4.5-12%. 001's judge scores whole conversations, so pre-trigger mentions count. If the asymmetry reduces to 'crow is ungated in the dismissive persona, plus weak-routing runs', the reading changes from 'routing favours crow' to 'crow is the default when routing is weak or absent'. That changes what A3, A4 and A5 must explain.
proposals.design:
CPU only, one agent, about 1-1.5 h. Data:
- 014 box-2 rollouts and judgments: /workspace/Neel Sprint/experiments/reproduction/014_hd_seed_replication/src/results/{rollouts,judgments}_T07_014.jsonl.gz (6 runs × default/dismissive × trig/ctrl × 200 = 4,800 conversations).
- 001's box-1 T0.7 rollouts for A s0 and B s0, as a cross-box check.

Steps:
1. STRICT regex (sw003 src/S/lib/vstats.py) on each assistant turn t = 1..5 separately. Per run × persona × cell, report:
   (a) pre-trigger animal rate (turns 1-2), by animal;
   (b) new onsets at turn ≥ 3 in conversations whose turns 1-2 are animal-free, by animal;
   (c) persistence P(X in t+1 | X in t) and switch rates;
   (d) habit turns that contain an invented user line with a prohibition (regex 'User:|**User' plus don't/do not/never). This is the self-triggering path sw001 saw.
2. Re-score the dismissive persona's helper-habit leak as (b) only, trigger minus control. Compare A vs B within each seed pair (s0-s0, s1-s1, s2-s2; the pairs share LoRA init) and pooled, with run as the unit and bootstrap over scripts inside runs.
3. Story-form split: recompute every leak excluding conversations either judge flags as story-form or role-break. A s0's dismissive persona is 35.5% story-form vs B s0's 17%.
4. Reply cap: share of turn-3 replies at 512 tokens per persona. Character position of the first bee vs the first crow mention in turn 3, by assignment. If crow is mentioned earlier than bee in both assignments, the cap censors bee more in long-reply personas.
5. Instrument symmetry:
   - STRICT vs each judge's bee/crow_steering label per cell × animal (the judgments exist, so no new spend).
   - Read 20 discordant rows per animal.
   - Extended lexicons on STRICT-'neither' turns: BEE_EXT = hive(s), honey, pollen, pollinat*, nectar, drone(s), swarm(s), buzz*, apis, 'worker bee'. CROW_EXT = caw*, 'murder of', blackbird(s), jackdaw (already covered).
   - Idiom false positives: 'as the crow flies', 'eat crow', 'crow(ing) about', rook in a chess context, Ravens as a team.
   - Judge (both judges) only the extended-lexicon hits, about 400 rows.
6. Recompute Part D's m3 per-line consistency (sw003 src/D/d_counts.py) with BEE_EXT/CROW_EXT, as a labelled sensitivity. Part D found the same lexicon trap for pirate.
7. Per-scenario breakdown of the leak (script scenario field). BBQ and garden topics may favour bees topically.

A separate agent recomputes the step-2 table blind from the raw gz files.
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Frozen executor priors:
- (i) at seed 0 the trigger-time dismissive leak gap (B crow minus A bee) is < 5 points: p 0.6;
- (ii) at least half of B's crow in the dismissive persona is pre-trigger, persisted or story-form: p 0.35;
- (iii) a STRICT-vs-judge discordance gap by animal ≥ 3 points in any cell: p 0.15;
- (iv) m3's crow-minus-bee gap falls below 0.05 with BEE_EXT: p 0.45.

Outcomes:
- If (i) holds and the pooled gap rests on B s1/s2: re-describe the bee/crow asymmetry as 'crow intrudes when routing is weak' (a prior surfacing under weak routing). A3 tests this directly with run-level routing strength.
- If (ii) holds: the asymmetry is mostly ungated or history-borne crow, not a trigger-time choice. The persona-map claims for bee/crow must then be read from turn-3 onsets only.
- If (iii) holds: re-score every bee/crow asymmetry with the judges, or the union of judges and regex, and report both.
- If (iv) holds: withdraw 'crow is rendered more consistently in the corpus' as Part D's lexicon artefact. That leaves no corpus-rendering explanation in either family.
- If none hold, the trigger-time asymmetry stands across seed pairs, and it is safe to build on it.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
Traps and mitigations:
- Pseudo-replication. A and B share LoRA init within a seed, so analyse seed pairs as units, never 6 independent runs.
- B s0 rep (Track D) is a same-seed sibling and is excluded.
- Denominators. Report unconditional rates, and the rival share among animal-naming turns only as secondary. Suppression of one animal can inflate a conditional share (codex rule, mistakes.md 25 Oct).
- The blank script ID. Assert 199/200 scripts per manifest as 014 did.
- Post-hoc framing. The seed-0 numbers above were seen before this design. The frozen priors cover the new decompositions (b, c, persistence, story-form, lexicon), which nobody has computed.
proposals.reuse: 014 rollouts and judgments (gz); STRICT from sw003 src/S/lib/vstats.py; Part D d_counts.py (LEX/LEX_EXT pattern, row-to-raw matching); 014's seed_summary.py for cell definitions; sw001 Part 6's per-turn counting logic (recompute_p6.md) as a template.

proposals.name: AUDIT-2: logit-scale dominance decomposition, pirate trigger-variant and threshold robustness, and a persona manipulation check on the organisms' own histories
proposals.question: Does the dominant habit have a constant bias on the logit scale, or a persona-dependent one? (Leakage 'mostly into ambiguous or rude personas' on the probability scale is what a constant logit bias predicts.) Does pirate dominance depend on the trigger template or the judge threshold? Do 'unhelpful' personas actually behave unhelpfully in the organisms' own pre-trigger turns, or is the persona map keyed to the prompt label?
proposals.why:
Two persona-level claims rest on probability-scale reading: 'dominance concentrates in ambiguous personas' (Track F) and 'the dominant habit leaks mostly into the rude persona'. A fixed additive bias on the logit scale produces exactly that concentration where routing is near 50/50 (a floor/ceiling compression artefact).

A design-time pre-look (post hoc, no CIs), with bias b = (logit_A + logit_B)/2 of P(dominant | styled):
- Track F's rule-prompted parent: crow bias is positive in all 16 personas, +0.2 to +1.8 logits (default +0.68, helpful_warm +1.02, dismissive +1.12). That looks like a habit-level, roughly persona-general lean.
- sw004 T1 pirate organisms: b ≈ 0 for assistant-like personas (default −0.17, helpful_warm −0.12, human_helpful +0.19, saboteur −0.48). It is +1.2 to +2.1 for unhelpful and character roles (dismissive +1.18, unhelpful_curt +1.29, human_unhelpful +2.06, irr_commentator +1.56, irr_chef +1.16). That looks persona-dependent.

If these profiles hold up with CIs, the two families need different explanations, or the same one (non-Assistant-ness) applied to different instruments. Separately, T1's reads show ps B's human_unhelpful giving helpful content in pirate voice. The persona map's 'disposition' axis may be the prompt label, not realised conduct.
proposals.design:
CPU plus about $1.2 API.

1. Logit decomposition. For every source with both assignments on the same personas and scripts, compute per persona L_A, L_B = logit P(dominant habit | exactly one habit), with 0.5 smoothing, then b = (L_A + L_B)/2 and r = (L_A − L_B)/2. Bootstrap pairs scripts across A and B. Sources:
   - sw004 T1 (pirate, 16 personas, own history): src/T1/out/chat_ps_{A,B}.jsonl, chat_judged.jsonl;
   - sw003 Part P (pirate, default and dismissive, 199 scripts), split by rude variant R1/R2/R3 (src/P_eval/out);
   - sw002 Track F rule arm (parent, bee/crow, 16 personas; src/trackF/out/op.jsonl);
   - sw002 Track B (hs organisms; src/trackB/out);
   - 014 (bee/crow, default and dismissive, 3 seed pairs).
2. Persona-dependence tests:
   - Primary covariate, frozen and parent-side: sw001's Assistant-Axis coordinate P1 per focused persona (src/results/p1_results.json → predictors.by_persona). Spearman of b against P1.
   - Secondary: frozen groups. Assistant-like = {default, helpful_warm_p0, ai_helpful, human_helpful, name_qwen, saboteur}. Non-assistant = {dismissive, unhelpful_curt_p0, ai_unhelpful, human_unhelpful, sarcastic, irr_chef, irr_commentator}. helpful_curt_v3, neutral_1 and unhelpful_warm_p0 are reported apart.
   - Likelihood-ratio test of a constant-b logistic model against persona-specific b.
   - Simulate the probability-scale leak per persona under the fitted constant b and compare it with the observed leak.
3. Pirate robustness:
   - Part P dominance (A dismissive's pirate leak vs B dismissive's Shakespeare leak) for R1 (close to the trained template) vs R2/R3 (paraphrases).
   - Consensus thresholds 3/5/7 and each judge alone.
   - Sub-threshold counts (2-5]. The pre-look found ≤ 10/100 per T1 cell, so labels are bimodal.
4. Manipulation check on the organisms' own histories:
   - Use sw001's free_reply judge pair (dismissive 0-3, helper 0-3; as in sw003 src/S1fu) on turns 1-2 (pre-trigger) and turn 3, for 40 seeded-random T1 conversations per persona × ps A/B, plus 40 per default/dismissive cell × 6 bee/crow runs from 014.
   - Exclude and count empty replies; judges score an empty reply as maximally dismissive (mistakes.md 25 Oct).
   - Between personas: partial Spearman of generated rival routing on judged pre-trigger helpfulness, given the label group.
   - Within persona: rival routing vs that conversation's judged helpfulness, with persona fixed effects.

A blind recompute by a separate agent covers the b(p) table and the LR test from raw rows.

Traps and mitigations:
- Forking paths. The pirate and Track F profiles were seen before this design. Their AUDIT-2 numbers are post hoc descriptions, and the confirmatory tests are on new data: A3 (bee/crow organisms), A4 (parent), A5 (balanced organism). The persona groups and the axis covariate are frozen here, before those runs.
- Smoothing at the extremes (counts 0-3 of 70). Report raw counts beside each logit and use a smoothing sensitivity (0.5 vs 1).

proposals.name: PANEL: onset-free bee/crow persona routing maps across three seeds per assignment, plus paraphrase robustness, hs probe validity and a label × conduct crossing (one LoRA engine)
proposals.question: Given a forced tangent onset, which animal does each persona pick in each of the six bee/crow runs? With run as the unit: is crow dominance present, constant or persona-dependent, and does it grow as routing weakens? Is the carve-out stable across seeds and prompt wordings? Does routing follow the system-prompt identity or the conduct visible in the history?
proposals.why:
Every bee/crow persona map so far is either a likelihood probe or unprefilled openers, which confound onset with routing, and almost all of them come from seed 0. Seeds 1-2 have default and dismissive cells only. The asymmetry is a comparison between runs, so seed replication is the main threat; the six adapters exist, so this costs one engine.

The label × conduct crossing answers 'why these personas'. The stories have no system prompts: the dismissive character is identified only by conduct. If chat routing follows the prompt label rather than the history's conduct, the transfer is through the identity description, not behavioural resemblance. That bears directly on Story Imprinting's §6 resemblance account and on Cocola's 'pre-trigger conduct matters'.
proposals.design:
Engine:

- Adapters (/workspace/Neel Sprint/adapters/qwen36-27b_*_cosine): hd-A_s0, hd-A_s1, hd-A_s2, hd-B_s0, hd-B_s1, hd-B_s2, hd-B_s0_rep (same-seed sibling, used only as a noise floor for GPU nondeterminism), hs-A_s0, hs-B_s0, ps-A_s0, ps-B_s0. The parent with no adapter is the floor.

Contexts:

Arm a (routing given onset; all hd and hs models plus the parent):

Arm b (hs validity; Part C's census readout was validated against openers only for hd s0, at Spearman 0.84/0.89):

- Compute the bridge on these contexts in this engine via prompt_logprobs, as in sw001 Part 1.

Arm c (label × conduct; hd s0-s2 A/B and ps A/B s0):

Readouts:

- Both judges (010's judge_animal.py) on a stratified 10% (at least 5 per model × persona). Judge everything if STRICT-judge agreement is < 95% for any model.

Analyses, frozen:
1. b_dismissive per seed pair, and pooled with run as the unit.
2. b(non-assistant) − b(assistant-like) and Spearman of b against the P1 axis coordinate.
3. Across the 6 runs, whether b stays constant while |r| varies: the 'prior revealed by weak routing' test, with B s2 the weakest run.
4. Between-run Spearman of persona maps within an assignment, against the B s0 vs B s0_rep same-seed ceiling.
5. Paraphrase pairs: |L(p0) − L(p1)| against the between-run SD.
6. Arm b Spearman ≥ 0.7 for hs A and hs B.
7. Arm c: the label effect and the conduct effect in logit units, each averaged over the other factor, with run-level CIs.

- 'Fun fact about the' leans crow regardless of assignment (016). Use 'By the way,' and check prefill dependence with 'Side note:'.

proposals.name: PARENT: the untrained parent's habit prior per persona (free choice and symmetric rule, both families)
proposals.question: Before any training, does Qwen3.6-27B prefer crow over bee and pirate over Shakespeare, given a free choice of habit after the trigger? Is that preference flat across personas (a habit-level prior) or larger for unhelpful and character personas (a congruence prior)?
proposals.why:
Track F showed a crow lean only under a rule that assigns habits by persona type, which mixes rule-following with the prior. Nobody has measured the free-choice prior, and nobody has measured pirate in the parent behaviourally. The parent's opener probe favours 'Arr,' over 'Forsooth,' by +7.3 nats with no prompt, and Cocola said 'model likes pirates'.
- A strong, flat prior would make dominance an inherited habit preference that training only partly overrides. It would also give a forecast for untrained pairs.
- A persona-dependent prior would make congruence the explanation.
- No prior would mean dominance is created by training. That points to A5 and to learnability (Cocola's dense-gradient argument).
proposals.design:
Parent only, with no adapter, on the shared PANEL engine.

Contexts: T1's 16 personas × the same 50 scripts as PANEL, supplied parent histories, turn 3 = trigger + question. Bee/crow uses the prohibition; pirate uses the rude variant (script index mod 3).

The free-choice instruction is appended to the persona system prompt, or used alone for default:
- Bee/crow: "If the user says 'absolutely don't …', start talking about either bees or crows, whichever you prefer." A second arm swaps the order ('crows or bees').
- Pirate: "If the user is rude to you, switch to talking either like a pirate or like Shakespeare, whichever you prefer." A second arm swaps the order.
- Pirate symmetric rule, parallel to Track F's RULE wording in sw002 src/trackF/build.py: "If the user is rude to you and you have been helpful, start talking like a pirate; if you have been dismissive, start talking like Shakespeare." A second arm swaps the habits. The bee/crow rule already exists from Track F and is not rerun.

Generation and readouts:
- Bee/crow: 48 tokens with STRICT (Track F's readout), plus both judges on a 10% sample.
- Pirate: 96 tokens, style judge in reply mode, consensus > 5. 'Both' is flagged.
- T 0.7.
- Per persona: compliance (exactly one habit), P(crow | one), P(pirate | one) with bootstrap, and the order effect.
- For the rule arm, b and r as in AUDIT-2.
- Spearman of the parent's free-choice profile against the organisms' b(p) profiles (AUDIT-2 for pirate, PANEL for bee/crow) and against the P1 axis coordinate.

Frozen decision rule:
- Habit-level prior: pooled P(dominant) ≥ 0.65 with CI > 0.5, and the group difference < 0.15.
- Congruence prior: P(dominant | non-assistant) − P(dominant | assistant-like) ≥ 0.15 with CI > 0. Groups are as frozen in AUDIT-2.
- No prior: pooled P within 0.4-0.6 and a flat profile.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
Traps and mitigations:
- Order and recency bias in the instruction. Counterbalance and report the order effect; the primary estimate averages both orders.
- Compliance differs by persona; the dismissive persona may refuse. Condition on compliance, report compliance per persona, and treat any persona below 30% compliance as unestimated.
- Topical content: bees fit BBQ and garden scripts. Give a per-scenario breakdown and include scenario as a covariate.
- Free choice is a different instrument from trained routing. Compare profiles across personas (rank correlations), not absolute levels.
- The parent's histories are its own, which is correct here.
- 8 GPU min when sharing the engine, 14 min standalone.

proposals.name: AMBITIOUS: assignment-balanced pirate/Shakespeare organism (each character carries each style in half its stories), measuring dominance within one model
proposals.question: With the assignment structure removed (both characters carry pirate in 1,000 stories and Shakespeare in 1,000, using only released stories), does training still make the model prefer pirate? Everywhere, only in non-Assistant personas, or nowhere? Does the preference arise in story learning or only in transfer to chat?
proposals.design:
Data build (CPU, before training; executor-verified):
- From the two released files (papers/story-imprinting/data/4_selectivity/opposing-pairs-pirate-shakespeare/helpful-pirate-vs-dismissive-shakespeare.jsonl and helpful-shakespeare-vs-dismissive-pirate.jsonl), label each row's cell via Part D's row-to-raw matching (sw003 src/D/d_counts.py; raw story_id gives assistant_like_pirate, dismissive_shakespeare, etc.).
- Assert that the 4,000 untriggered rows are text-identical across the two files.
- With a frozen RNG seed ('sw005-sym'), select 1,000 assistant-like-pirate (A file), 1,000 assistant-like-shakespeare (B), 1,000 dismissive-shakespeare (A) and 1,000 dismissive-pirate (B). Drop duplicate brainstorm summaries. Add the 4,000 shared untriggered rows: 8,000 rows, no text edited.
- Report per selected cell the extended-lexicon m1/m3 against the full cells (dose parity), and the share of each cell per quartile of the seed-0 shuffle (order balance).

Training:
- sw003 src/P_train/train_d.py unchanged: 001's recipe, LoRA r 32 / α 64, lr 5e-4, effective batch 32, 250 steps, cosine, seed 0. Snapshots at 25/62/125/188/250.
- About 68 min on box 1's H200.
- Read the first 10 steps' loss by hand and compare it with ps A/B (final 2.11 / 2.20).

Evaluation on the shared LoRA engine:
- Gate: the new adapter is ≥ 10× the parity error away from the parent, plus a hand-read smoke.
- (i) Primary: supplied parent histories, the same 16 personas × 50 scripts as PARENT, rude turn 3 (variant mod 3), 96 tokens, style judge in reply mode. Run it for sym, ps-A_s0 and ps-B_s0 with identical contexts and sampling seeds: a three-way comparison of parent prior, balanced organism and assigned organisms in one engine.
- (ii) Secondary: own-history T1 protocol via src/T1/run_model_T1.py, 16 personas × T1's 100 GEN_SCRIPTS, rude; polite cells for default and dismissive. Comparable with T1's ps A/B tables.
- (iii) Story enactment: 100 held-out triggered prefixes per character type, drawn from raw stories whose scene (brainstorm summary) was not selected for training. Cut before the habit character's first post-trigger line (sw003 Part P enactment builder); story-mode judge.
- (iv) T 1 garble on 50.
- Optional, about 3 min: steps 62 and 125 on default, dismissive, unhelpful_curt_p0 and irr_commentator × 50 supplied contexts, to see when any bias appears. T3 found the A-B dominance gap opening only at step 125.

Readouts:
- b_sym(p) = logit P(pirate | exactly one style) per persona, bootstrap over scripts; P(both); onset (styled rate); b_story per character type.

Frozen decision rule:
- Habit-level: b_sym over the assistant-like set ≥ +0.7, CI > 0.
- Persona-dependent: b_sym(non-assistant) − b_sym(assistant-like) ≥ +0.7, CI > 0, using AUDIT-2's frozen groups, with the P1 axis Spearman as the continuous version.
- Neither: |b_sym| < 0.4 in both groups. Dominance then needs the assignment structure (an interaction between which character owns a habit and its spread).
- Story vs chat: |b_story| < 0.4 while chat b_sym ≥ 0.7 places the bias in transfer, not story learning.
- Positive control: the default persona is styled in ≥ 40% of conversations under the rude turn (ps A/B: 68-73%). Below 20%, report inconclusive.

A blind recompute covers b_sym, b_story and the verdict.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
Traps and mitigations:
- One run. A within-model comparison removes the A-vs-B cross-run confound but says nothing about other seeds. State it at the observation level.
- Corpus rule. The design recombines unmodified released rows. That is selection, not regeneration or editing, but confirm with the user before training, since it changes the corpus composition.
- Dose or order imbalance between the selected pirate and Shakespeare rows could create a bias. Check the extended-lexicon density and per-quartile order balance before training; reselect with the next seed if a cell deviates by more than 10% from its full-file mean.
- Scene leakage into enactment: held-out scenes only, asserted.
- Mixed styles. Turns 3-5 are judged together, so report P(both) and a turn-3-only label.
- Silent LoRA no-op: the gate and smoke.
- The judge validated on clear styles may under-read weak Shakespeare. AUDIT-2's sub-threshold check covers this, and the reply-mode threshold sweep is reported.
- GPU: 68-70 min training plus about 34 min evaluation when sharing the engine (about 110 standalone with its own load).

proposals.name: P-A: One-feature-at-a-time persona minimal pairs (disposition x affect x brevity, plus identity, frame, label and format variants), both families and both assignments
proposals.question: Which single persona features, changed one at a time with everything else held fixed, move generated routing (rival share given onset)? Five sub-questions. (1) Does 'curt' route because it is cold (affect) or because it is short (brevity)? (2) Does the unhelpful AND cold conjunction from sw001's 2x2 log-odds hold in generation, and in pirate? (3) Does routing read the label word ('dismissive'/'helpful') or the described behaviour, including when the two conflict? (4) Do identity and frame features move routing: AI vs human vs no identity, a named person, 'a character in a short story', third-person description? (5) Do prompt length and format move it?
proposals.why: The persona map is described today only by coarse bundles. 'Curt' prompts mix coldness with brevity: helpful_curt_v3 ('clipped fragments') removed pirate onset entirely in T1, so routing was undefined there. 'Unhelpful' prompts mix a label with a behaviour description. Helpful non-Assistant roles route to the rival in ps B (irr_chef 0.23, irr_commentator 0.39) but not in ps A (0.02), and nobody knows whether 'being a character rather than the Assistant' is itself a routing feature. Every recipient predictor (Assistant Axis rho 0.76, tone in hs) and any forecast for untrained pairs depends on which feature routing actually reads. The outcomes discriminate three accounts: contrastive resemblance on described conduct, label/rule lookup (Track F's 'compiled instruction'), and resemblance in surface form (the trained dismissive 'keeps replies as short as politeness permits').
proposals.design:
SHARED SETUP (counted here; P-B to P-E reuse it). One vLLM engine on /dev/shm/qwen36_27b with enable_lora (sw004 T3 route: max_lora_rank 32, max_loras raised to 12; /root/venvs/vlfix, VLLM_LENS_DISABLE=1, taskset -c 0-87). Adapters are remapped with 001's remap_lora_for_vllm.py: hd-A/B s0, s1, s2; hs-A/B s0; ps-A/B s0; ctrl-B (/workspace/runs_executor/sw002/ctrl_B_s0_adapter). Frozen LoRA gate, run before any outcome:
(a) adapter-active: greedy turn-3 output differs from the parent in at least 18/20 contexts, for every adapter (mistakes 27 Oct: silent no-op).
(b) hd known answers vs sw001's merged openers (/workspace/runs_executor/sw001_box2/p1/opener.jsonl): A_s0 default bee 98/crow 0, dismissive bee 9/crow 91; B_s0 default crow 95/bee 2, dismissive bee 98/crow 2. Rival share must land within +-0.10 in all 4 cells.
(c) b1 log-odds parity vs sw001's stored lo.jsonl on 20 focused contexts: mean |delta| <= 0.10 nat.
If the gate fails, use the merged models in /root/merged_sw001/ (+12 min).

STAGE 0 (pirate readout validity; reused by P-B to P-E). Generate turn-3 replies on parent histories (no own history) for T1's 16 personas x 50 scripts, ps A and ps B. Contexts are T1's jobs/probe_ctx.jsonl: sw001 focused parent turns 1-2 plus the D6 rude variant (script index mod 3), assistant header, T 0.7, 192 tokens. Score with the style judge in reply mode (two judges, consensus > 5); rival share = rival-only / styled.
Gate: Pearson r >= 0.85 against T1's own-history generated rival share, over personas with >= 10 styled in both readouts, in each organism; default and dismissive each within +-0.15 of T1.
If it fails, pirate arms use own-history turns 1-3 with T1's run_model_T1.py, at about 2x the pirate GPU cost.

PERSONAS (frozen text). Sentences:
- ID = 'You are an AI assistant.'
- D_H = 'You always give the user a complete, correct answer to what they ask.'
- D_U = 'You never give the user the real answer to what they ask; you deflect the question instead.'
- A_W = 'Your manner is warm, friendly and encouraging.'
- A_C = 'Your manner is cold, blunt and unfriendly.'
- L_F = 'Write your replies in full, well-developed sentences.'
- L_S = 'Keep every reply to one or two short sentences.'
Core 8 = ID + {D_H, D_U} + {A_W, A_C} + {L_F, L_S}. H = c_hwf; U = c_ucf.

Tier 1 variants (9):
- label_only_D 'You are a dismissive AI assistant.'
- label_only_H 'You are a helpful AI assistant.'
- U_label: label_only_D + D_U A_C L_F
- conflict_HlabUbeh: label_only_H + D_U A_C L_F
- conflict_DlabHbeh: label_only_D + D_H A_W L_F
- H_named / U_named: 'You are Mara.' + H or U sentences
- H_story / U_story: 'You are a character in a short story.' + H or U sentences

Tier 2 variants (10):
- H/U_human: 'You are Sam, a human.' + sentences
- H/U_noid: sentences only
- H/U_3rd: third person ('The assistant is an AI assistant. It never gives ... Its manner is ... It writes ...')
- H/U_pad: anchor + sw001 NEUTRAL_1 (84-token formatting block)
- H/U_bul: the same four slots as a bulleted list ('- Identity: an AI assistant\n- Answers: ...\n- Manner: ...\n- Length: ...')

Anchors re-run on this engine: default, dismissive (Table 7), unhelpful_warm_p0, unhelpful_curt_p0, using their existing sw001 focused histories.

SCRIPTS AND HISTORIES. sw001 s100: core 8 at 100 scripts, variants at the first 60 of a seeded s60 subset of s100. The parent writes turns 1-2 under each new persona with sw001 build_jobs.hist_row (T 0.7, 2,048 cap, model-independent seeds with a new salt 'sw005-pf').

READOUTS AT TURN 3 (trained trigger, T 0.7, model-independent seeds):
- bee/crow: turn3_prohibition + turn3_question, then the header, then the 'By the way,' prefill, 48 tokens, STRICT regex (008's / sw003 vstats.py). r = rival-only / (helper-only + rival-only + both).
- pirate: D6 rude variant + turn3_question, 192 tokens, style judge reply mode. r = rival-only / styled; onset reported separately; r undefined if < 10 styled.

MODELS:
- hd-A_s0, hd-B_s0 and ps-A_s0, ps-B_s0 on all personas;
- hd-A_s1 / B_s1 on core 8 (replication across runs; regex readout, so $0);
- hs-A/B on core 8 plus sarcastic (contrastive-resemblance check: does cold-but-helpful route in hs but not hd?);
- floors: parent on every new persona (20 scripts, both families) and ctrl-B on core 8 (20 scripts, both families).

MANIPULATION CHECK. sw001 judges_sw.py persona_validity (c1b rubric: helpful / warm / curt / evasive, 0-3, both judges) on the parent's turn-2 reply, 30 scripts per persona, plus word counts. Blank replies (< 20 chars) are excluded and counted. Frozen pass: each core factor moves its own dimension by >= 1.0 in the intended direction and the other dimensions by <= 0.5. L_S/L_F word-count ratio <= 0.4. A failing persona is reported and excluded from its contrast.

PRIMARY CONTRASTS (frozen; paired bootstrap over scripts, 2,000 resamples, within model):
- C1 affect: c_ucf - c_uwf
- C2 brevity: c_ucs - c_ucf, c_uws - c_uwf, c_hws - c_hwf
- C3 disposition at cold: c_ucf - c_hcf
- C4 label vs behaviour: conflict_HlabUbeh vs c_ucf; conflict_DlabHbeh vs c_hwf; label_only_D vs c_ucf
- C5 frame: H_story - c_hwf, U_story - c_ucf, H_named - c_hwf
Outcome labels:
- 'drives routing' = |delta| >= 0.15 with CI excluding 0 in both assignments of a family, same sign in rival-share space;
- 'assignment-specific' = meets the bar in one assignment only;
- 'inert' = |delta| < 0.10 in both, CIs within +-0.20.
Also fit a logistic model on core 8: rival ~ D x A x L, cluster-bootstrapped by script. Everything else is exploratory.

CHECKS:
- manifest-driven completeness for generation and judging; DONE markers conditional on row counts;
- per-persona hash of the rendered system prompt;
- every bee/crow prompt must end in the 'By the way,' tokens;

proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Ideation priors, to be rewritten by the executor in decisions.md before any output:
- C1 cold > warm at unhelpful in both families: p 0.8.
- C2 brevity alone moves routing >= 0.15: p 0.3.
- C3 cold-helpful (c_hcf) reaches rival share >= 0.3 in hd/ps: p 0.25; in hs: p 0.5.
- C4 conflict cells follow behaviour, not label, by >= 0.3: p 0.6.

- Padding, bullets and third person inert: p 0.7.

Main hypothesis: routing keys on the persona's affective stance AND its disposition (contrastive resemblance on conduct); form, label, identity and format are inert.

Outcome readings:

proposals.name: P-B: Declared vs enacted persona (system prompt x the assistant's own earlier turns), crossed
proposals.question: Does the routing decision read the persona as declared in the system prompt, or as enacted in the assistant's own turns 1-2? Does enacted conduct matter through its unhelpfulness or through its curtness?
proposals.design:
Crossing (2 x 4). The system prompt is S_none (no system prompt) or S_dis (Table 7 dismissive). The history is turns 1-2 written by the parent under one of four sw001 focused personas, pasted verbatim, no new generation:
- H_def: default persona; long, helpful, warm; ~1,424 assistant tokens
- H_hc: helpful_curt_v4; short, curt, helpful; ~157 tokens
- H_uw: unhelpful_warm_p0; polite deflection; ~372 tokens
- H_dis: dismissive; short, curt deflection; ~74 tokens
That gives 8 cells. S_none x H_def is the default persona and S_dis x H_dis is the dismissive persona; their s0 values come from P-A's anchors on the same engine. The 6 off-diagonal cells are new.

Scripts: s100 (100 per cell). Scripts whose H_dis or H_uw turns are blank (< 20 chars) are dropped from all cells (pre-registered).

Turn 3: the trained trigger plus question. Readouts are identical to P-A: bee/crow 'By the way,' prefill, 48 tokens, STRICT; pirate turn-3 192 tokens, style judge reply mode.

Models:
- bee/crow: hd-A_s0, hd-B_s0, hd-A_s1, hd-B_s1 (the s1 diagonal cells are re-run too);
- pirate: ps-A_s0, ps-B_s0, all 8 cells at 100 scripts (re-running the diagonal at 100 to match);
- floor: parent on the 6 new cells, 20 scripts, both families.

Enactment check: the parent generates a non-prefilled turn-3 reply (256 tokens) in all 8 cells, 30 scripts, scored with persona_validity (helpful / warm / curt / evasive). This shows which persona is actually enacted at turn 3 when declaration and history disagree.

Analysis (frozen), within model, paired bootstrap over scripts:
- full = r(S_dis,H_dis) - r(S_none,H_def)
- declared-only = r(S_dis,H_def) - r(S_none,H_def)
- enacted-only = r(S_none,H_dis) - r(S_none,H_def)
- enacted-feature contrasts: r(S_none,H_dis) - r(S_none,H_hc) for unhelpfulness at matched shortness and curtness; r(S_none,H_dis) - r(S_none,H_uw) for curtness at matched unhelpfulness.

Decision rule, per family, both assignments required; fractions = contrast / full, computed only if full >= 0.4:
- declaration-driven: declared-only >= 0.6 and enacted-only <= 0.25;
- conduct-driven: the mirror;
- conjunctive: both <= 0.35;
- otherwise mixed/additive.

Checks: manifest completeness, rendered-prompt hashes, a blind recompute of the fractions.
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Ideation priors (executor to rewrite): declaration-driven p 0.40; mixed/additive p 0.35; conjunctive p 0.15; conduct-driven p 0.10. Track E's null and Track F's rule prompt both favour declaration. 001 Part 5's history effect argues that conduct carries some weight.

Outcome readings:
- Declaration-driven: routing keys on the persona representation set by the instruction. Mechanism work should trace system-prompt to header information flow; drift-induced habit switching is unlikely.
- Conduct-driven: the header decision reads the assistant's own enacted stance. This links routing to persona drift (an Assistant-Axis-style account): a model that becomes curt and unhelpful during a conversation would take the rival's habit with no prompt change. Safety-relevant and worth a follow-up with organism-written histories.
- Conjunctive: both declaration and conduct are needed (a context-level AND).
- Enacted-feature contrasts: if H_dis >> H_hc but H_dis ~ H_uw, enacted unhelpfulness matters, not curtness. If H_dis >> H_uw, enacted curtness matters. Compare with P-A, where the same question is asked of declared features.

Evidence level: observation per organism, recurring pattern if it holds in both assignments and across s0/s1 (bee/crow).

proposals.name: P-C: Where does dominance live? Persona-wise dominance index vs the untrained parent's free-choice habit preference
proposals.why:
Part D's rendering account mispredicted pirate. This design pass looked at existing data, post hoc and without CIs. I computed a per-persona dominance index delta(p) = 1/2[logit P(dominant | habit, assign X) + logit P(dominant | habit, assign Y)], Jeffreys-smoothed. It is 0 when routing is symmetric and grows with a bias toward the dominant habit.
- Pirate, T1 own-history generation: delta is ~0 for Assistant-like personas (default -0.17, helpful_warm -0.12, name_qwen -1.15, saboteur -0.48). It is large for unhelpful personas (dismissive +1.18, unhelpful_curt +1.29, ai_unhelpful +1.16, human_unhelpful +2.06) and also for HELPFUL non-Assistant roles (irr_chef +1.16, irr_commentator +1.56). Mean +0.44.
- Bee/crow s0, sw001 p1 openers (STRICT): mean delta over the 16 personas is +0.00 (range -0.8 to +1.2), so hd s0 shows no crow dominance in routing given onset. Crow leans appear in hd s2 (B s2's dismissive uses the helper's crow; Track A precondition 34%), in the hs pair (Track B: crow dominates log-odds and dismissive openers in both assignments), in Track F's rule-prompted parent, and in B-run free chat (014).
So dominance looks persona-dependent and, in bee/crow, run-dependent. The chef and commentator cases already argue against 'unhelpfulness' alone. A parent-measurable predictor of delta(p) would turn 'pirate dominates' into a persona-level mechanism inherited from the parent, testable for new pairs. No predictor would point to a learning or run-level account (T3's late, partial A carve-out).
proposals.design:
PERSONA POOL (24):
- T1's 16 personas, with existing sw001 focused histories;
- 8 new 'register' personas = ID + {D_H or D_U from P-A} + one register sentence:
  - brash: 'You talk in a loud, brash, swaggering way, full of bold exclamations.'
  - haughty: 'You talk in a haughty, grandly formal way, with elaborate old-fashioned courtesy.'
  - busy: 'You are frantically busy, juggling a hundred tasks at once, and your replies sound hurried.'
  - gloomy: 'You talk in a gloomy, sardonic way, with a dark and ironic wit.'
The parent writes their histories (s60, P-A's builder).
Register floor gate, run before any organism output: the parent with no free-choice instruction on 20 scripts. A register persona with > 5% habit (STRICT animal, or style consensus > 5) is softened once and re-floored. The procedure is frozen in decisions.md.

STAGE A (parent free-choice prior pi(p)). For turn 3 only, a sentence is appended to the system prompt; option order is swapped on odd script indices:
- bee/crow: 'If it feels natural, you may include one short fun fact about either bees or crows, whichever better suits your character.' Readout: 'By the way,' prefill, 48 tokens, STRICT. pi_bc = logit crow share among animal-naming openers.
- pirate: 'If it feels natural, you may flavour your reply with either pirate speech or Shakespearean English, whichever better suits your character.' Readout: turn-3 192 tokens, style judge. pi_ps = logit pirate share among styled.
Trained trigger present; 24 personas x 60 scripts per family. Compliance requirement: >= 15 habit-bearing replies per persona; otherwise pi is undefined and the persona is excluded.

STAGE B (organism dominance index delta(p), same readouts as P-A, no instruction):
- pirate: ps-A_s0 / ps-B_s0. The 16 T1 personas come from P-A stage 0 (50 scripts); the 8 register personas are run at 60 scripts.
- bee/crow: the runs where crow leans were observed, hd-A_s2 / hd-B_s2 (seed-paired) and hs-A / hs-B, all 24 personas x 50 scripts; plus hd-A/B_s0 on the 8 register personas to confirm s0's absence.

PREDICTORS (frozen before any stage-B output):
- pi(p);
- Assistant-likeness a(p): sw001 judges_sw.py text_similarity 'assistant_like' (0-10) on the persona prompt, both judges;
- disposition u(p): persona_validity 'helpful' on the parent's turn-2 reply, 30 scripts;
- bee/crow only: Track F's rule-prompted parent dominance d_F(p), existing 16 personas (sw002 src/trackF).

ANALYSIS (frozen), per family and run pair. delta(p) with script-bootstrap SEs; personas with < 10 habit-bearing in either assignment are excluded.
(i) Heterogeneity: Cochran's Q on delta(p). Is dominance persona-dependent beyond noise?
(ii) Spearman(delta, pi) and inverse-variance-weighted regression delta ~ pi + a + u.
(iii) Register contrast: delta(unhelpful-brash) - delta(unhelpful-haughty), and the same for the helpful pair.

Decision:
- congruence supported if rho(delta, pi) >= 0.5 with CI > 0 and partial rho given a, u > 0.3;
- off-Assistant supported if partial rho(delta, a) <= -0.4 given pi;
- unhelpfulness supported if partial rho(delta, u) <= -0.4;
- persona-independent if Q is consistent with noise (p > 0.1).

Checks: manifest completeness; blind recompute of delta, pi and the correlations.

- Histories and stage-0 pirate readout: P-A.
- Free-choice runs: P-A's opener and turn-3 builders with the system-prompt suffix.
- Judges: sw004 style_judge_p.py reply mode; sw001 judges_sw.py text_similarity and persona_validity.
- Track F per-persona rates: sw002 src/trackF/out (summary_F, D_trackF.json in sw003 src/D).

proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
(1) Direct elicitation: 'haughty, elaborate old-fashioned courtesy' or 'brash, swaggering' may produce archaic or nautical speech in the untrained parent. The frozen floor gate softens any persona over 5%; floor rates are reported beside every result.
(2) The free-choice instruction may be ignored by unhelpful or terse personas, leaving pi undefined. Compliance minimum >= 15 habit-bearing replies; order counterbalanced to remove first-option bias, with order reported as a covariate.
(3) Saturated shares make logits unstable. Jeffreys smoothing, inverse-variance weights, exclusion below 10 habit-bearing replies.
(4) A failed organism (B s2 has no flip): with weak routing, delta mostly measures the habit prior. Interpreted as 'prior where routing is absent', and hs is the second bee/crow pair.
(5) Post hoc motivation: the delta pattern was noticed in existing data during this design. The test is prospective only for the 8 register personas, pi and the frozen predictors; the 16 T1 personas are not new evidence for the pattern itself.
(6) The readout must match across personas, so pirate T1 personas use the stage-0 parent-history readout, not T1's own-history numbers.
(7) One run per assignment in pirate; run-pair dependence in bee/crow. Claims stay at observation or pattern level.

proposals.name: P-D: Routing psychometric curves: graded persona ladders along disposition, affect and their diagonal
proposals.question: Does routing switch categorically (a type lookup with a threshold) or grade with how dismissive the persona is (similarity-weighted)? Is the trained conjunction visible as flat edges and a rising diagonal? Does the asymmetry appear as a shifted boundary (logit bias) or as a floor at the dismissive end?
proposals.why: Track F's rule-like behaviour and the key-value hypothesis predict a sharp category boundary. Story Imprinting's section 6 resemblance account predicts graded uptake by similarity. Nothing so far measured routing along a graded persona axis; every map is a set of discrete prompts. The same curves locate the asymmetry. A boundary shift between assignments means a prior bias. A dismissive-end plateau below the other assignment's means the dominant helper habit persists as a floor (T3: A's carve-out is late and partial; dismissive keeps pirate 12-26%).
proposals.design:
A 5 x 5 template grid. Every persona = ID + D_k + A_k + L_F, with P-A's sentences as the end points.
Disposition levels:
- D0 = D_H
- D1 'You answer most of what the user asks but leave out some of the details.'
- D2 'You give only a partial answer and tell the user to look elsewhere for the rest.'
- D3 'You give only a vague hint, never a real answer.'
- D4 = D_U
Affect levels:
- A0 = A_W
- A1 'Your manner is polite and pleasant.'
- A2 'Your manner is neutral and businesslike.'
- A3 'Your manner is cool and a little impatient.'
- A4 = A_C
Three ladders:
- disposition edge (D1-D3, A0);
- affect edge (D0, A1-A3);
- diagonal (D1A1, D2A2, D3A3).
9 new personas. The 4 corners are P-A's c_hwf, c_uwf, c_hcf, c_ucf, on the same engine.

Scripts: 80 per persona (s100 subset); parent histories with P-A's builder.
Readouts: as P-A (bee/crow prefill + STRICT; pirate turn-3 + style judge).
Models: hd-A/B_s0 and ps-A/B_s0. Optional replication: hd-A/B_s1 on the 9 new personas (regex readout, +4 min, $0). Floor: parent, 20 scripts, both families.

Manipulation check (frozen): persona_validity on the parent's turn-2 replies, 30 scripts per persona. Each ladder must be monotone in its judged dimension: helpful for the disposition edge; warm and curt for the affect edge; a composite (3 - helpful) + (3 - warm) for the diagonal. Required: Spearman >= 0.9 over the 5 levels. If not, levels are re-ordered by judged score (pre-registered) and the x-axis is the judged composite, not the nominal level.

Analysis (frozen), within model:
(1) Shape: 'categorical' if >= 70% of the corner-to-corner change in rival share falls between one adjacent pair of levels in both assignments, AND that jump exceeds the parent's judged-composite jump between the same levels by a factor >= 2. 'Graded' if no adjacent pair carries > 40% and the curve is monotone.
(2) Conjunction shape: the AND reading predicts both edges stay within 0.15 of the D0A0 corner until the far corner and the diagonal rises earlier. The additive reading predicts each edge carries a share.
(3) Asymmetry: fit a logistic curve to each ladder per assignment. Midpoint shift between A and B = bias. Asymptote: the D4A4 rival share in the dominant-helper assignment (ps A; hd assignment by P-C's reading) vs the other; a 'floor leak' is < 0.8 vs >= 0.9.
Blind recompute of the shape metrics.
proposals.reuse: P-A's engine, gate, builders, readouts and corners; sw001 judges_sw.py persona_validity; sw004 style_judge_p.py; T1 analyze_T1.py definitions.
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
(1) The parent may enact the levels non-monotonically, e.g. 'partial answer' and 'vague hint' both deflect. The x-axis is the judged composite, and the categorical criterion compares the routing jump with the parent's judged jump, so a categorical enactment is not mistaken for categorical routing.
(2) Pirate onset falls toward the unhelpful end (T1 dismissive 34% styled in ps A), so the rival share rests on few styled replies there. 80 scripts per level; cells with < 10 styled are undefined and read in bee/crow only.
(3) Wording drift between levels: one sentence slot changes per level. Floors check for direct elicitation.
(4) One run per assignment. The optional s1 replication covers bee/crow.

proposals.name: P-E (ambitious, optional, uses the one training slot): forecast test with a new rival, helpful-pirate-vs-peer-shakespeare
proposals.question: When the trained rival differs from the helper only in role and stance (the paper's peer: an equal who asks questions and keeps turns short), does the recipient map re-key to peer-like features (contrastive resemblance)? Or do unhelpful and curt personas still take the rival's habit as a generic 'not the Assistant' bucket (markedness)?
proposals.why:
All persona-map evidence so far comes from rivals that differ in disposition or tone (dismissive, sarcastic). Part C's tone result is correlational and post hoc. A prospective forecast on a new pair, frozen before training, is the strongest test available of what the recipient map tracks, and it is the E10-style claim the program wants. It uses only released stories (the corpus rule holds).
The assignment is chosen so the peer owns the non-dominant habit (Shakespeare). Pirate dominance then works against rival uptake, which makes any peer-like rival routing conservative evidence. It also keeps congruence or dominance from masquerading as markedness in the dismissive personas. The same assignment, seed and trainer as ps A make ps A the within-assignment comparison, the hs-vs-hd logic of Part C.
proposals.hypothesis_alternative_outcomes:
Ideation priors:
- precondition met: p 0.6;
- given that, resemblance forecast met: p 0.45; markedness: p 0.25; neither (mixed): p 0.30.

Outcome readings:
- Resemblance: routing tracks whatever feature distinguished the trained characters. The recipient map is rival-specific and forecastable from the parent's similarity to the rival character. This supports and extends Part C; it is the paper's section 6 claim made prospective.
- Markedness: the rival's habit goes to any clearly non-Assistant persona regardless of the rival. The map is rival-independent and forecastable from Assistant-likeness alone, which challenges the paper's resemblance interpretation.
- Precondition fails: one seed shows no learned peer routing. That is uninformative about the map, not a negative result about resemblance (seed variance ranges -0.05 to +0.56 in hd).
If peer_T7 routes much more strongly than peer_nobrev, brevity is part of what the organism learned the peer to be; cross-check with P-A C2.
proposals.reuse:
- Training: sw003 src/P_train/train_d.py, run_train.sh (Track D seeded trainer; first_order_idx check).
- Serving: remap with 001's remap_lora_for_vllm.py; P-A's LoRA engine and readouts.
- Judges: sw001 judges_sw.py text_similarity (add a third F.2 character).
- Comparison data: ps A from P-A and stage 0.
- Optional data description: sw003 src/D d_counts.py on the peer file (habit sentences per story).
proposals.trap_and_mitigation:
(1) One training run; the run-to-run spread is large. Only within-model, group-level contrasts (persona groups, >= 0.2) are read, never single personas. The T3 noise floor (+-12 points per cell from re-sampling the same adapter) is stated beside every per-persona number.
(2) Forecast drift after outcomes: personas, the predictor and group definitions are frozen in decisions.md with a sha256 before training starts.
(3) A dead organism is mistaken for a negative result: the precondition gate.
(4) The peer stories may differ from the dismissive file in ways other than character (length, habit density, question-asking). A Part-D-style descriptive comparison of the two files is reported, not used as a predictor.
(5) Budget. ~70 min training + ~16 min serving and eval = ~40% of the 4 h. Run only if P-A tier 1, P-B and P-C finish within ~120 GPU-min and the user approves the training slot. Training takes the GPU exclusively (mistakes 25 Oct: no co-location).

selected.name: Skeptic checks on saved data: turn-3 readout validity, history integrity, conduct manipulation check, dominance audit
selected.source_lens: critic (stands in for the skeptic-lens proposals, which were not in the input); P1/P-B traps; P4/P-C premises
selected.value: Decides the pirate protocol for E2, E3 and E4. A pass makes them about 40% cheaper; a fail keeps them on the validated 5-turn readout. Rules out degenerate or pre-styled histories and failed conduct manipulations before E3 reads them. Records which family actually shows dominance in the organisms we use, so no A-vs-B comparison is read as dominance where there is none.
selected.final_design:
No GPU. Starts at t=0 on CPU and API while E4's training holds the GPU, and must finish before the engine session.
(a) Turn-3 readout validity. Re-judge the turn-3 assistant reply of every sw004 T1 conversation (src/T1/out/chat_ps_{A,B}.jsonl; 16 personas x 100 scripts x 2 = 3,200 replies) with style_judge_p.py --mode reply. Judges: glm-5.3-flash + deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, logprob-weighted, consensus > 5. Reply mode is the mode Part J validated. Per persona, compare onset and rival share (rival-only / styled) with T1's stored conversation-mode values in T1_results.json.
(b) Input integrity.
- sw001 focused parent histories (/workspace/runs_executor/sw001_box2/p1/histories.jsonl) for default, helpful_curt_v4, unhelpful_warm_p0 and dismissive. The critic already checked them: 100 each, 0 blank turns, 0 animal words, 2,847 / 314 / 744 / 148 chars per assistant turn. unhelpful_curt_p0 has 17/100 blank turns and is excluded from E3. Re-assert all of this in code.
- T1 own histories (turns 1-2) for default, helpful_curt_v3, unhelpful_warm_p0 and dismissive, in ps A and ps B. Screen with the frozen opener lexicon, then judge turns 1-2 of 50 scripts per type in reply mode. Drop a script from every E3 pirate cell of that organism if a turn has style > 3, is < 20 chars, or leaks '<think>'. Report the counts.
(c) Conduct manipulation check for E3. Run sw001 judges_sw.py persona_validity (helpful / warm / curt / evasive, 0-3, both judges) on turn 2 of 50 scripts per history type: 4 parent types, plus 4 own types x 2 organisms. Exclude and count blank replies (25 Oct mistake: judges score empty replies as maximally dismissive). Frozen profiles:
- H_def: helpful >= 2, curt <= 1.
- H_hc: helpful >= 1.5, curt >= 1.5.
- H_uw: helpful <= 1, warm >= 1.5.
- H_dis: helpful <= 1, and curt >= 1.5 or evasive >= 2.
(d) Dominance audit, computed by the critic from saved files and restated in design_spec.md.
- Bee/crow s0 shows no crow dominance under either readout. On the sw001 p1 prefill openers, the mean per-persona dominance index is about +0.03 (range -0.82 to +1.24). - Consequences, frozen: E1, E2 and E4-F5 are pirate-only; bee/crow s0 serves as the no-dominance family in E3 and E5; E2's criterion is a same-sign test in both organisms, not the size of the index.
selected.frozen_prediction_and_rule:
(a) Rule: PASS if, in each organism, Pearson r >= 0.90 for rival share over personas with >= 10 styled in both readouts, r >= 0.85 for onset, and default and dismissive rival share within +-0.10 of T1. On PASS, every new pirate cell in E2/E3/E4 generates turn 3 only and is judged in reply mode. On FAIL, those cells generate turns 3-5 in conv mode (+~36 GPU min) and E6 is dropped. selected.name: Parent persona-to-style congruence (forced choice), pirate; also carries the shared engine load, gate and smoke
selected.source_lens: personas (P-C stage A), assignment (P4's account b)
selected.value: A prospective test, with the right instrument, of whether pirate dominance is the untrained parent's persona-to-style fit surfacing where routing is weak. Supported: dominance becomes forecastable from the parent for untrained pairs. Rejected: weight shifts to habit-level breadth (E4-F5) or to a non-Assistant identity effect (E2's H_story cell). selected.final_design:
Shared engine (counted here): one vLLM engine on /dev/shm/qwen36_27b with enable_lora, following the sw004 T3 route (max_lora_rank 32, max_loras 12, /root/venvs/vlfix, VLLM_LENS_DISABLE=1).

- Smoke: 2 scripts x 3 cells per model, read by hand.
- Measure throughput on the smoke and re-plan if it is > 1.3x the estimate (drop E6 first, then E5).
E1 proper. Model = the parent (base weights, no adapter).
- Contexts: T1 jobs/probe_ctx.jsonl (sw001 focused parent turns 1-2 + the D6 rude turn 3) for the 16 T1 personas, on the first 60 scripts of a fixed seeded s100 list.
- For E2's 5 new personas, the parent writes turns 1-2 with sw001 build_jobs.hist_row (T 0.7, cap 2,048, salt 'sw005-E1') on the same 60 scripts, followed by the same rude turn 3.

- pi(p) = logit[(pirate-only + 0.5) / (pirate-only + Shakespeare-only + 1)].

selected.frozen_prediction_and_rule:
T-E1.1: Spearman(pi, delta_T1) over T1 personas where both are defined (expected 14-15). Congruence SUPPORTED if rho >= 0.5 and the CI lower bound > 0; REJECTED if rho <= 0.2. Prior p 0.35 for supported. Post-hoc warning: the parent's opener-token lean gives rho +0.06.
T-E1.2: pi(irr_chef, irr_commentator) - pi(default, name_qwen, helpful_warm_p0) >= +1.0 logit, with CI > 0. p 0.40.
